prior_value.label: VERDICT REACHABILITY DECLARATIONS — owner pins 148, 42
prior_value.pin: 148 — the two golden-tile blocks declare first
prior_value.method: Pin 42 keyed on a self-declared `kind: gate` that appears ZERO times in this store, so it never inspected anything (pin 140). These declarations state, per block, the condition under which each verdict could occur and which one did — by forward pointer, so no witnessed node is edited
prior_value.why_these_two_first: anchor-gate check 2 RUNS NOTHING: it is discharged by citation to phase14.stage0.gate2_loader_identity and to the golden tile. A cited gate that could never have fired makes the citation hollow, and check 2 is one of two cited checks under the identity chain
prior_value.finding: NOT hollow. Both golden-tile legs FIRED — mu by 6.23x and map rms by 4.10x over their recorded tolerances — and the scale check's discriminator is an equality against an independent artifact (phase13_lane0_mean.nc), so its other verdict was reachable too

phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.cited_by: phase14.stage1.anchor_gate.checks.loader_identity — check 2 runs nothing and is discharged by citation to this block and to phase14.stage0.gate2_loader_identity
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.pass_condition: |mu_delta| <= 0.002 AND map rms <= 0.010 m — the recorded thresholds
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.fail_condition: either leg over its threshold; both legs are one-sided tolerances on a measured difference, so either verdict was available before the numbers existed
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.outcome_observed: FAILED BOTH LEGS, which is why the bridge caveat exists
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.why_not_unfailable: the two legs are independent tolerances on measured differences between two data lineages; a repackaging-only difference would have landed inside both. They did not, by 6.2x and 4.1x, and the failure is the finding the tabled row carries forward

phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.cited_by: the same check-2 citation; this sub-block is what rules out solver drift as the explanation of the mu delta above
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.pass_condition: side A reproduces the SIGNED solution (mu_a 0.76941 vs lane0 0.76953 on the their_eval scale, 1.43 cm rms against phase13_lane0_mean.nc) -> the delta is a SCALE mismatch, not drift
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.fail_condition: side A does NOT reproduce the signed solution -> solver drift, and the whole A-vs-B comparison becomes uninterpretable
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.outcome_observed: scale mismatch CONFIRMED, no solver drift
phase14.stage0.golden_tile.dc2021a_vs_cm.why_not_unfailable: the discriminator is an equality against an independent recorded artifact, not a property of the comparison itself: had the generalized path drifted, mu_a would not have matched lane0 and this check would have said so

epoch_classes.no_deduplication_note: EVERY epoch's constellation is UNIQUE — 15 epochs, 15 distinct mission sets, still 15 after removing the locked c2/c2n. THE PRICE HAS NO CHEAP REDUCTION AVAILABLE. A reader will otherwise assume one exists (owner pin 234b).

obs_scaling.independent_corroboration: phase14.stage1.tier2_probe_kuroshio_m100.derived_pin_89d.wall.implied_exponent = 1.28, whose verdict_on_the_anchors already recorded 'NOT linear ... optimistic by 1.42x'. v1's flat model was FLATTER THAN LINEAR, which this project's own pinned evidence had already rejected once.

projection_declaration.what_it_may_be_used_for: MAGNITUDES ONLY, declared as projected. The DIRECTION of the subset ordering does NOT rest on this fit — it is a counting fact (owner pin 239a/b).

probe_cross_check.why_not_the_price: CONVERGED and admissible, but it is a ONE-WINDOW PROJECTION of the thing the legs then MEASURED, and the measurement supersedes it. Its value now is as a RECORD OF HOW A ONE-WINDOW PROJECTION PERFORMED.

projection_declaration.outcome_when_tested: OVER-PREDICTED by 1.574x against the direct nine-window measurement of the same tile

full_sweep_range.why_a_range: A SINGLE NUMBER WOULD HIDE A 1.4x SPREAD THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE TILES, NOT OF THE OSSE (owner pin 236c). 'A tile solve' is not one number: the four measured legs run 19.67-27.48 h.
full_sweep_range.which_tile_is_an_open_input: WHICH TILE AN OSSE WOULD USE IS NOT DEFAULTED HERE (236d). The choice belongs with the run decision.

constellation_size_is_an_open_input.statement: ⛔ WHICH CONSTELLATION AN OSSE RE-SOLVE RUNS IS AN OPEN INPUT, NOT A DEFAULT — and it is the LARGER axis. The epoch classes run 3 to 9 missions against the legs' 5, a per-class spread of roughly 4.7x, against the tile axis's 1.40x.
constellation_size_is_an_open_input.v1_defect: v1 declared the SMALLER axis open while collapsing the BIGGER one (owner pin 239d).

ordering_is_a_counting_fact.why_exponent_free: post-lift has FEWER classes (6 vs 9) and MORE total missions (44 vs 35). Under ANY cost monotone in observation count it is dearer. ONLY the flat 'one class = one leg' model reverses it, and that model is what the review overturned.
ordering_is_a_counting_fact.magnitudes_are_projected: the HOURS carry obs_scaling's pin-139 declaration; the DIRECTION does not depend on the fit (owner pin 239a/b)

v1_editorial_WITHDRAWN.withdrawn_text: The cheapest subsets are cheap precisely because they drop the epochs the era-transfer claim is weakest at. Cost and evidential value move together here.
v1_editorial_WITHDRAWN.why: IT WAS AN ARTEFACT OF THE FLAT MODEL AND INVERTS WITH IT. The sparse historical constellations — exactly where era-transfer is weakest — carry the FEWEST observations and are therefore the CHEAPEST classes to solve.
v1_editorial_WITHDRAWN.not_replaced: ⛔ NOT replaced with the opposite editorial (owner pin 239c): that would be the same mistake with a different sign. The inversion is recorded as a FINDING; no claim is made about cost and value moving together or apart.

query.authorisation: owner pin 237(a) — metadata only, no download, one host
query.no_total_volume_field: the STAC document carries NO total-size field; the volumes below are DERIVED from itemSize x grid geometry. That derivation rests on two typed geometry assumptions (the bbox and node-inclusive counting) and on the UNCOMPRESSED array size, so it is a bound on the wire volume rather than a wire measurement (reviewer defect 4)

truth_field.variable: zos (sea surface height) — the OSSE truth field
truth_field.scope_assumption: zos only. No MDT, mask or ancillary fields are costed — adequate for a nadir-SLA OSSE, stated as a scope choice, not an omission
truth_field.bbox_caveat: this is the SOLVE box. Simulating observations needs truth over the OBS footprint (solve bbox + the 1.0 deg operative halo = 21 deg), which is (21/19)**2 = 1.22x larger. NOT applied here because the obs-footprint choice belongs with the run design; stated so the figure is read as the SOLVE-box volume it is
truth_field.window_plan_shape: 9 windows x 60 d on a 45-d stride — OVERLAPPING by 15 d, NOT contiguous; 540 window-days over a 400-d union. The UNION is the download basis because each day is bought once
truth_field.does_not_scale_with_classes: THE TRUTH FIELD IS BOUGHT ONCE PER TILE, NOT ONCE PER CLASS. An OSSE varies the CONSTELLATION over FIXED model truth, so N_epoch-classes multiplies the RE-SOLVES and not the truth download. It DOES scale with the number of tiles.

feasibility.derived_not_asserted: the verdict is computed from the volume against the budget, so shrinking the budget flips it
feasibility.why: the spec's 'heavy downloads' is true of the GLOBAL FULL RECORD (0.20 TiB of zos alone) and NOT of the tile-and-span subset an OSSE needs

lower_bound.statement: THE FIGURES HERE ARE A LOWER BOUND ON THE OSSE PRICE — INCLUDING THE COMPUTE FIGURE ITSELF.
lower_bound.compute_is_itself_a_lower_bound: ⛔ WIDENED UNDER OWNER PIN 239(e). v1 attributed the lower bound to uncosted ENGINEERING alone, so a reader concluded the compute band was sound. IT IS NOT: the flat model under-prices every class above 5 missions, and 7 of the 15 classes are above it.
lower_bound.what_is_covered: constellation-varied re-solves + the truth download, both at declared model assumptions
what_is_not_costed: truth-provider wiring: the TRUTH interface is DORMANT since 4b and re-arming it is unmeasured engineering time
per-class observation simulation from the truth field
non-convergence retries: the legs ran 424-554 PCG iterations at 5 missions; the 3-mission classes are sparser, worse-conditioned and outside anything measured
calendar time and box occupancy: these are serial single-host hours, with a launch gate of 2x predicted peak RSS per class
lower_bound.why_unmissable: Owner pins 237(d) and 239(e): an OSSE priced at re-solves alone understates it, and pin 235(b) named that as the most likely error. The gap is BOUNDED on the download axis and OPEN on both the engineering and the compute-model axes.

m_100_predicted_not_measurable_by_splitt.extrapolation_declared: EXTRAPOLATION on the m axis, and the field name says so: splitting a 100-member ensemble yields halves of 50, so m=100 is the one value the method cannot measure. The form is checked at m=25 and m=50 against pooled means and by an independent Monte-Carlo route, and applied at m=100 on that basis — a validated FORM, not a measured point

predicted_T_cross.extrapolation_declared: EXTRAPOLATION on the CRN-STATE axis, which is the axis nobody wrote down: the number is computed at the pre-T14 measured r and used to predict behaviour after T14 pairs the draws by construction. r post-T14 is UNMEASURED — T14 has not run, and it is Stage 2's under pin 88's halt. Pin 68(b) already fixes the direction (T_cross must FALL, and a fall is NOT evidence of repair); the magnitude is what this axis cannot supply
predicted_T_cross.quantity: T_cross under rho = r^2, as the sharpened T14 prediction

predicted_T_cross.note: evaluated AT the measured r, so this number crosses nothing. The r ~ 0.9 application of the same model IS an extrapolation and is declared at phase14.stage1.rho_model_range_limitation (validated_range [0, 0.2523], application_range [0, 0.9]) — the one block in this store that ever declared itself
predicted_T_cross.quantity: T_cross under rho = r^2 at the MEASURED r
